notes: Prose contract: cases are proven by each language's own tests keyed to these ids. Promoting cases to executable vectors requires extending tools/spec_coverage_gate.py and every language runner to per-capability coverage reports in the same change. Id families: 1xx strict validation, 2xx legacy-mode equivalence, 3xx precedence/composition, 4xx redaction, 5xx source behavior. Error codes CFG-001..004 are defined in spec/config.md and are distinct from these test ids.

tests.title: Missing required key fails closed
tests.given: Strict-mode construction with the client group requested and no source yielding client.discovery_url or client.id
tests.then: No Config value is produced and a CFG-001 error names each missing required logical key

tests.title: Incomplete client group fails closed
tests.given: Strict-mode construction where a client-group key (client.id) is supplied but client.discovery_url is absent
tests.then: No Config value is produced and a CFG-002 error names group 'client' and the missing key

tests.title: Missing client secret for a secret-requiring auth method
tests.given: Strict-mode construction with a complete client group except client.secret, and a client-auth method selected that requires a secret
tests.then: No Config value is produced and a CFG-002 error names group 'client' and client.secret

tests.title: Invalid value fails closed, never silently defaults
tests.given: Strict-mode construction where a source yields a non-numeric http.timeout and an out-of-domain http.retry.max_attempts
tests.then: No Config value is produced and a CFG-003 error names each invalid logical key; the registry default is not substituted

tests.title: Empty or whitespace-only string is present-but-invalid
tests.given: Strict-mode construction where a source yields an empty string for a typed key and a whitespace-only string for another
tests.then: Each yields CFG-003 (present-but-invalid); emptiness is never treated as absence

tests.title: All construction errors are collected and reported atomically
tests.given: Strict-mode construction with a missing required key, an invalid value, and an incomplete group simultaneously
tests.then: Exactly one failure is reported carrying all errors ordered by registry order, and no Config value exists

tests.title: Uniform boolean parsing
tests.given: Strict-mode construction with boolean-typed keys set to TRUE, false, 1, 0, and yes
tests.then: true/false/1/0 parse case-insensitively; 'yes' yields CFG-003

tests.title: Absent optional keys take registry defaults
tests.given: Strict-mode construction with only the required client-group keys supplied
tests.then: client.scope is 'openid profile email', client.audience equals client.id, client.post_login_redirect and client.post_logout_redirect are '/', client.excluded_paths is ['/docs','/openapi.json','/health'], http.timeout is 30.0

tests.title: Constructed Config is immutable
tests.given: A successfully constructed strict-mode Config
tests.when: Mutation of any field is attempted through the language's public surface
tests.then: Mutation is impossible (compile-time or runtime per language idiom); changed configuration requires constructing a new value

tests.title: Strict mode harmonizes 0 cache entries as unbounded
tests.given: Strict-mode construction with jwks.cache.max_entries = 0
tests.then: The typed value records the documented unbounded semantics (0), identically in every language

tests.title: URL keys must be absolute with a scheme
tests.given: Strict-mode construction where client.discovery_url is a schemeless or relative string
tests.then: CFG-003 names client.discovery_url; scheme policy (https-only) follows the consuming component's existing rules and is not weakened by configuration

tests.title: Legacy TTL resolution: invalid to default, out-of-range clamps
tests.given: Legacy-mode resolution of jwks.cache.ttl and discovery.cache.ttl with garbage, NaN, below-minimum, and above-maximum raw values
tests.then: Garbage/NaN yield the defaults (86400 / 3600); numeric values clamp to [60, 86400] — matching today's Python behavior bit-for-bit

tests.title: Legacy cache-entry cap divergence is preserved per language
tests.given: Legacy-mode resolution of jwks.cache.max_entries with raw values '0', '-5', 'abc', '', and unset
tests.when: The values are resolved in each language
tests.then: Python yields 64 for all of them (0 is NOT unbounded); Go and Rust yield 64 for '-5'/'abc'/''/unset and 0 (unbounded) for '0' — each language reproduces its own current behavior exactly

tests.title: Legacy retry alias precedence
tests.given: Legacy-mode resolution of http.retry.max_attempts with HTTP_RETRY_MAX_ATTEMPTS and HTTP_RETRY_COUNT set in combination
tests.then: The primary wins when both are set; the alias is honored when only it is set; '0' is honored as retries-disabled

tests.title: Legacy TLS chain order
tests.given: Legacy-mode resolution of the TLS verify source with combinations of SSL_CERT_FILE, CURL_CA_BUNDLE, and REQUESTS_CA_BUNDLE set
tests.then: The first set variable in the order SSL_CERT_FILE, CURL_CA_BUNDLE, REQUESTS_CA_BUNDLE wins; none set falls back to system CAs — matching today's Python behavior including the REQUESTS_CA_BUNDLE compat shim

tests.title: Legacy kid-miss cooldown semantics
tests.given: Legacy-mode resolution of jwks.kid_miss_cooldown with garbage, negative, above-maximum, and '0' raw values
tests.then: Garbage yields the default 5.0; numeric values clamp to [0, 3600]; '0' is honored as the documented opt-out

tests.title: Legacy resolution preserves read timing
tests.given: A library code path whose environment read happens at call time today
tests.when: The read site is migrated to legacy-mode resolution
tests.then: Resolution still occurs at the same call site (no hoisting to construction), so a mid-process environment change behaves exactly as before; proven by the language's pre-existing test suites passing unmodified

tests.title: Explicit override wins over every source
tests.given: A key set via explicit override and different values for it in a custom source and the environment
tests.then: The override value is used; sources are not consulted for that key

tests.title: Earlier source wins over later source
tests.given: Two consumer-supplied sources yielding different values for the same key
tests.then: The value from the source listed first is used

tests.title: EnvSource is implicitly last and can be repositioned
tests.given: A consumer-supplied source plus the environment both yielding a key, and separately an explicit source list placing EnvSource first
tests.then: By default the custom source beats the environment; with EnvSource explicitly listed first, the environment wins

tests.title: Registry default applies only when no source yields
tests.given: A key yielded by no source and another key yielded by a low-precedence source
tests.then: The unyielded key takes the registry default; the yielded key takes the source value, not the default

tests.title: Alias resolves within a source before falling through
tests.given: A higher-precedence source yielding only the alias env name and a lower-precedence source yielding the primary env name
tests.then: The higher-precedence source's alias value wins; within a single source the primary wins over the alias

tests.title: Debug and display output redacts secrets
tests.given: A constructed Config containing a secret-classified value
tests.when: The Config is rendered via the language's native debug/display mechanisms
tests.then: Output contains the placeholder '<redacted>' for the secret and never the raw value

tests.title: Serialized output redacts secrets
tests.given: A constructed Config containing a secret-classified value
tests.when: Any serialization the Config type offers is produced
tests.then: Serialized output contains '<redacted>' for the secret and never the raw value

tests.title: Errors name keys, never values
tests.given: A strict-mode construction failure involving keys whose supplied values are known sentinel strings (secret and non-secret)
tests.then: The message contains logical key ids and error codes but none of the sentinel values

tests.title: Raw secret access is explicit
tests.given: A constructed Config containing a secret-classified value
tests.then: The raw value is reachable only through an explicit accessor (expose/Value per language idiom), never via implicit string conversion

tests.title: Unknown keys from a source are discarded
tests.given: A source returning the requested keys plus keys not in the registry
tests.then: Unknown keys are silently ignored; requested keys resolve normally; no error is raised

tests.title: A failing source fails construction closed
tests.given: A source whose resolve operation raises/errors
tests.then: No Config value is produced and a CFG-004 error identifies the failing source; the source is not silently skipped

tests.title: Sources are consulted exactly once per construction
tests.given: A counting source supplied to strict-mode construction
tests.then: The source's resolve operation was invoked exactly once and received the registry key list (bulk snapshot; no per-key pulls)
